items.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020
items.q: people like Chuck and then John Audino and Ray Triscari, all these guys had known me through Buddy’s band and through Woody’s band

ctx.x: You should have just said, “Well it’s talent man, come on.”

Yeah. No I wouldn’t do that. No the thing was they’d got me in and people like Chuck and then John Audino and Ray Triscari, all these guys had known me through Buddy’s band and through Woody’s band and through things like that, they knew who I was. And so they said, “Hell yes.” And the contractors said okay. And of course when you show up you’ve got to play and I could read really well and I had decent chops. I had limitations but I didn’t let anybody know what they were you know.

I wonder if you could get real specific for me, because I’ve been curious about — you show up, first of all you get a call from the contractor, and they tell you the studio and the time. Do you get any other information like make sure you have your mutes? Bring your flugelhorn? Or are you just expected to know that part of it?
